links.note: The sum of a polygon's exterior angles is 360 degrees - the total measure the pentagon-walking activity was set up to produce, quoted back as a fact.

Each exterior angle 45 degrees gives 360/45 = 8 sides. Going from the exterior angle to the number of SIDES is exactly what this concept says exterior angles are good for; 31294 is the 360 total itself.
Each exterior angle of a regular 9-gon is 360/9 = 40 degrees: the total measure shared equally, so it is the total that is being used.

The false option denies that a rectangle's opposite sides are equal. All four options are rectangle properties (equal angles, no obtuse angle, bisecting diagonals, equal opposite sides), which is this concept's content.

The false option denies that a square's diagonals cut it into four equal parts; the other three are the square-as-rectangle, square-as-rhombus and perpendicular-bisecting-diagonals facts this concept gathers.
A:B = 1:2 in a parallelogram gives A = 60 only because A + B = 180. The supplementary-adjacent-angles property is the whole step.
The false option claims all four sides of a kite are equal. A kite has two distinct pairs of equal CONSECUTIVE sides, not four equal sides - this concept's definition.
All four sides equal names it a rhombus; the 120/60 adjacent angles are there to stop it being called a square. All-sides-equal is this concept's definition.
Angle C equals angle A = 60 degrees because they are opposite angles of a parallelogram - straight application of the equal-opposite-angles property, with 120 offered as the adjacent-angle trap.
The angle adjacent to 65 degrees is 115 degrees: adjacent angles of a parallelogram add to 180.

A rhombus is a parallelogram, and in general parallelogram diagonals are NOT of equal length, so the statement is false. 31304 is the concept that states non-equality; 31308 gives perpendicular bisection, which does not settle equality.

Decides whether every regular polygon passes the convexity test, so the operative definition is the convex/concave one. NOTE: the marked key 'False' is wrong - a regular polygon is necessarily convex. See report.
The false option is 'all parallelograms are rectangles', reversing the inclusion. A rectangle is defined here as a parallelogram with every angle right, which is what makes the reversal fail.

Two diagonal lengths fix a rhombus and nothing else, because a rhombus's diagonals are perpendicular bisectors of one another - give the two lengths and the figure is determined. That property is this concept.
The fewest-sided polygon is a triangle, which follows from what a polygon is - a simple closed figure of line segments needs three. (Option 'Angle' is not a polygon at all.)
The sum of a polygon's exterior angles is 360 degrees - the same total measure as qid 113488, differently worded.
Interior angle 108 gives exterior 72 and so 360/72 = 5 sides. Using knowledge of the exterior angle to get at the interior angle and the number of sides is this concept word for word.

Equal sides, equal angles AND equal diagonals together single out the square - the intersection of the rhombus and rectangle cases that this concept describes. A rhombus fails on diagonals, a rectangle on sides.
The pentagon's 108 degree interior angle makes the target exterior angle 36, hence 360/36 = 10 sides, a decagon. Both halves move between interior and exterior angles and the side count.

Angle A of the trapezium comes out as 180 - 65 = 115, which works only because the trapezium has a pair of parallel sides making those two angles co-interior. The pair-of-parallel-sides definition is what the figure turns on.
